university: The University of Texas at Tyler

documents.title: Artificial Intelligence Language for Syllabi
documents.stance_why: The page requires every instructor to 'identify to what degree students may utilize' AI and supplies three categories (encouraged; permitted for specific assignments; not permitted) with sample statements. The university sets no single rule and hands the choice to instructors, so delegates with tiers.
tiers: AI is encouraged during the course, and appropriate acknowledgement is expected
AI is permitted only for specific assignments or situations, and appropriate acknowledgement is required
AI is not permitted in this course at all
documents.summary: Academic Affairs requires every UT Tyler syllabus to carry standard AI language (acknowledge all AI use, no protected data, verify output, misuse is an integrity breach) plus one of three instructor-chosen categories. Each category has sample statements, with citation, appendix and Honor Code details.

units.why: Faculty 'must identify to what degree students may utilize' AI, so every instructor has to state AI expectations; instructor actor, set before the course, must, and P09 because the duty is to state it in the syllabus.
units.anchor: must identify to what degree students may utilize artificial intelligence (AI) tools

units.why: The page defines 'three basic categories for using AI tools', i.e. named tiers; admin-authored framing, informs, P05 for named categories.
units.anchor: There are three basic categories for using AI tools

units.why: The sample statements are 'suggestions' and the instructor 'can create a statement', so the rule is set per instructor; P04, modality may.
units.anchor: These are suggestions; you can create a statement for appropriate use in your course.

units.why: Faculty are asked to 'consider the nature of the course, discipline, and student learning objectives' when choosing a category, tying the AI decision to learning objectives (P83).
units.anchor: consider the nature of the course, discipline, and student learning objectives

units.why: Instructors 'need to be very clear' about expectations, a duty to communicate rules to students; P09 as the closest communicate type.
units.anchor: You need to be very clear about your expectations about appropriate use of AI tools

units.why: 'Required language for each UT Tyler syllabus' makes an AI statement mandatory in every syllabus: P09.
units.anchor: There is required language for each UT Tyler syllabus

units.why: Instructors 'need to include the appropriate category' in the 'About this Course' section, which fixes where the statement goes; P09.
units.anchor: include the appropriate category of artificial intelligence language use for your course

units.why: The university 'pre-populated' the required language in the syllabus module, an administrative set-up fact supporting the syllabus-statement duty; P09, informs.
units.anchor: The required syllabus language has been pre-populated

units.why: Instructors 'can repeat the required syllabus language' alongside the course category; optional detail of the syllabus-statement procedure, so P09 with may.
units.anchor: you can repeat the required syllabus language

units.why: The required statement opens with an institutional commitment 'to exploring and using' AI 'as appropriate for the discipline and task', a framework principle (P56) rather than a rule; unit stance is encouraging.
units.anchor: UT Tyler is committed to exploring and using artificial intelligence (AI) tools

units.why: 'We encourage discussing AI tools' ethical, societal... implications' asks the community to talk about AI beyond listing rules, matching P66 (discuss AI in class); P53 does not fit because it names harms, not discussion.
units.anchor: We encourage discussing AI tools’ ethical, societal, philosophical, and disciplinary implications.

units.why: 'All uses of AI should be acknowledged' is a disclosure duty tied to the Honor Code; P24, should because of the word 'should'.
units.anchor: All uses of AI should be acknowledged

units.why: Faculty and students 'must not use protected information, data, or copyrighted materials' with AI: a data-protection ban. P50 chosen over P49 because it covers faculty and data too.
units.anchor: must not use protected information, data, or copyrighted materials when using any AI tool
units.fit_note: Also covers copyrighted materials, which P50 does not name.

units.why: AI content 'may appear correct but is sometimes shown to be incomplete, inaccurate... and/or biased' warns that output is unreliable: P31, informs.
units.anchor: content that may appear correct but is sometimes shown to be incomplete, inaccurate

units.why: AI 'should not be considered a substitute for traditional approaches to research' says AI must not replace the student's own research thinking; P32 is closest, though it is about research method specifically.
units.anchor: should not be considered a substitute for traditional approaches to research
units.fit_note: Concerns research approaches rather than problem-solving in general.

units.why: 'You are ultimately responsible for the quality and content' of submissions makes students own what they submit: P29.
units.anchor: You are ultimately responsible for the quality and content of the information you submit.

units.why: Misuse that violates course guidelines 'is considered a breach of academic integrity', classifying it as misconduct: P36.
units.anchor: is considered a breach of academic integrity

units.why: Students 'will be subject to disciplinary actions as outlined in' the Academic Integrity Policy, sending misuse to the integrity process (P36); P37 does not fit because no concrete penalty is named.
units.anchor: subject to disciplinary actions as outlined in UT Tyler’s Academic Integrity Policy

units.why: The template leaves a slot for each instructor to 'insert appropriate AI Category of Use', so the course rule is set per instructor: P04.
units.anchor: insert appropriate AI Category of Use and statement for your course

units.why: This is the heading of the first of three named categories ('AI is encouraged... acknowledgement is expected'), so it is a tier definition: P05.
units.anchor: AI is encouraged during the course, and appropriate acknowledgement is expected.

units.why: Sample statement: 'I encourage you to explore using... AI tools... for all assignments and assessments' welcomes AI by default: P02.
units.anchor: I encourage you to explore using artificial intelligence (AI) tools, such as ChatGPT

units.why: 'Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited' requires a citation with each submission using AI: P24.
units.anchor: Any such use must be appropriately acknowledged and cited

units.why: The citation must include 'the specific version of the tool used', a tool-detail requirement, so P25 rather than generic P24.
units.anchor: including the specific version of the tool used

units.why: Students 'should include the exact prompt' and 'complete response as an appendix', which is a transcript submission: P26 (P25 would cover only the citation detail).
units.anchor: include the exact prompt you used to generate the content and the AI’s complete response

units.why: Students 'must assess the validity and applicability of any submitted AI output' because it may be inaccurate: P31.
units.anchor: you must assess the validity and applicability of any submitted AI output

units.why: 'You will not earn full credit' if AI-sourced content is inaccurate states a grade penalty in advance; P37 is nearest.
units.anchor: You will not earn full credit if inaccurate, invalid, or inappropriate information
units.fit_note: A grade reduction for inaccurate content, not a sanction for misconduct.

units.why: Sample statement 'You can use AI programs (ChatGPT, Copilot, etc.) in this course' allows AI by default: P02.
units.anchor: You can use AI programs (ChatGPT, Copilot, etc.) in this course.

units.why: The sample calls AI 'powerful tools for learning' that save time, generate ideas and personalize learning, naming benefits without a rule: P87.
units.anchor: powerful tools for learning and other productive pursuits

units.why: AI use does not change duties: students 'must follow UT Tyler's Honor Code', i.e. existing university policy applies (P77).
units.anchor: You must follow UT Tyler’s Honor Code and uphold the highest standards of academic honesty.

units.why: Uncited content is treated the same 'whether created by a human or in collaboration with an AI tool', equating AI with a human source: P45.
units.anchor: whether created by a human or in collaboration with an AI tool

units.why: Students 'must cite the tool's contribution', a disclosure duty: P24.
units.anchor: you must cite the tool’s contribution to your work

units.why: 'Students can use AI platforms to help prepare for assignments' is a general permission with the work itself still done by the student; P02.
units.anchor: Students can use AI platforms to help prepare for assignments and projects.

units.why: 'You can use AI tools to revise and edit your work' permits editing support: P91.
units.anchor: You can use AI tools to revise and edit your work

units.why: Students 'must identify any writing, text, or media generated by AI' on submission: P24.
units.anchor: students must identify any writing, text, or media generated by AI

units.why: AI-generated sections 'should appear in a different colored font', marking AI content at the place it appears: P27.
units.anchor: sections of assignments generated by AI should appear in a different colored font

units.why: The relationship between AI and student contributions 'should be discussed in a cover letter', a written reflection on AI use: P26.
units.anchor: discussed in a cover letter that accompanies the assignment when submitted

units.why: Heading of the second named category ('permitted only for specific assignments'), a tier definition: P05.
units.anchor: AI is permitted only for specific assignments or situations, and appropriate acknowledgement is required.

units.why: 'When AI use is permissible, it will be clearly stated in the assignment directions' commits the instructor to state permission per assignment (P09).
units.anchor: it will be clearly stated in the assignment directions

units.why: 'All use of AI must be appropriately acknowledged and cited' is a disclosure duty (this wording repeats in Example 3 and is coded once): P24.
units.anchor: all use of AI must be appropriately acknowledged and cited

units.why: 'Otherwise, the default is that AI is not allowed during any stage' sets the rule when the assignment is silent: P06.
units.anchor: the default is that AI is not allowed during any stage of an assignment

units.why: AI is 'limited to assignments where AI is a critical component', so it is allowed activity by activity: P04.
units.anchor: AI will be limited to assignments where AI is a critical component

units.why: 'Learning how to use AI is an emerging skill' justifies in-course AI use as a skill to learn: P44.
units.anchor: Learning how to use AI is an emerging skill

units.why: The instructor commits to 'always indicate when and where' AI is appropriate, an expectation-communication promise: P09.
units.anchor: I will always indicate when and where the use of AI tools

units.why: Students must 'add an appendix showing... the entire exchange (e.g., prompts used)': a transcript requirement (P26).
units.anchor: add an appendix showing (a) the entire exchange (e.g., prompts used)

units.why: The appendix must describe 'precisely which AI tools were used', tool-level detail: P25.
units.anchor: a description of precisely which AI tools were used

units.why: The appendix must explain 'how the AI tools were used', a reflection on use (P26).
units.anchor: an explanation of how the AI tools were used

units.why: The appendix must give 'an account of why AI tools were used', a reflection on motives (P26).
units.anchor: an account of why AI tools were used

units.why: 'Students shall not use AI tools during in-class examinations or assignments unless explicitly permitted' bans AI in in-class assessment: P22.
units.anchor: Students shall not use AI tools during in-class examinations or assignments unless explicitly permitted

units.why: Example 4 promises students will be 'notified as to when and how' AI will be used, a communicate-expectations commitment: P09.
units.anchor: You will be notified as to when and how these tools will be used

units.why: AI use outside stated parameters 'violates UT Tyler's Honor Code, constitutes plagiarism': classified as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: violates UT Tyler’s Honor Code, constitutes plagiarism, and will be treated as such

units.why: Heading of the third named category, 'AI is not permitted in this course at all': a tier definition, P05.
units.anchor: AI is not permitted in this course at all.

units.why: 'I expressly forbid using ChatGPT or any other AI tools for any stages of the work process, including brainstorming' bans AI outright: P01.
units.anchor: I expressly forbid using ChatGPT or any other artificial intelligence (AI) tools

units.why: 'All work students submit... to be their own' makes students own what they submit: P29.
units.anchor: I expect all work students submit for this course to be their own.

units.why: Own work without AI 'is best for your efforts in mastering course learning objectives': a skill-building rationale, P41.
units.anchor: Doing your own work, without human or artificial intelligence assistance, is best

units.why: Deviations 'will be considered a violation of UT Tyler's Honor Code', so breaches go through integrity processes: P36.
units.anchor: will be considered a violation of UT Tyler’s Honor Code and academic honesty values

units.why: Example 2 requires graded work 'by yourself' and says the exclusion 'includes artificial intelligence (AI)': a default ban, P01.
units.anchor: This exclusion of other resources to help complete assignments includes artificial intelligence (AI).

units.why: 'Refrain from using AI tools to generate any course context (text, video, audio, images, code)' forbids having AI produce submitted work: P19.
units.anchor: Refrain from using AI tools to generate any course context

units.why: Submitted work 'will be generated by themselves' requires students' own authorship (P29).
units.anchor: The work submitted by students in this course will be generated by themselves.

units.why: The rule 'includes all process work, drafts, brainstorming artifacts, editing' extends the AI ban to every stage, a default ban: P01.
units.anchor: This includes all process work, drafts, brainstorming artifacts, editing, and final products.

units.why: Using 'AI tools (such as ChatGPT)' is listed with contract cheating as an Honor Code violation, i.e. misconduct (P36).
units.anchor: using AI tools (such as ChatGPT)

units.why: The page states it 'was adapted from AI Syllabus information from Carnegie Mellon University, Stanford...', describing how the guidance was made: P84.
units.anchor: This document was adapted from AI Syllabus information from Carnegie Mellon University

units.why: The authors disclose they used 'Grammarly, an AI tool for writing' on this document, modeling disclosure of staff AI use: P47.
units.anchor: This document was edited for grammar using Grammarly, an AI tool for writing.

documents.title: AI Guidelines & Policies
documents.stance_why: The page points faculty to the required syllabus language ('must specify the extent to which students are permitted to use' AI) and itself sets data, tool and legal rules rather than a stance on student AI use. Academic-work decisions are left to the instructor ('not allowed by the instructor'), so delegates.
documents.summary: Digital Learning guidance lists approved Microsoft AI tools, allows ChatGPT-type tools only with public data, and bans sensitive or confidential data, unauthorized output, grading and decision-making uses. It adds responsible-use, privacy and enforcement notes and asks faculty to use the syllabus language.

units.why: Faculty 'must specify the extent to which students are permitted to use' AI, an obligation to state AI rules per course: P09.
units.anchor: must specify the extent to which students are permitted to use artificial intelligence (AI) tools

units.why: Faculty are asked to 'include the provided... Syllabus language', the standard statement in every syllabus: P09.
units.anchor: Please include the provided Artificial Intelligence Syllabus language.

units.why: The page's preamble states purpose and principle ('clear guidelines and a shared commitment to ethical practice'): P56.
units.anchor: Responsible AI use starts with clear guidelines and a shared commitment to ethical practice.

units.why: Copilot and Azure Open AI 'are available AI tools with contractual agreements for use by UT Tyler': the institution's approved tools, P92 (not P17, which is course-specific).
units.anchor: are available AI tools with contractual agreements for use by UT Tyler

units.why: 'We highly recommend against using Bing Copilot on sensitive data sets' protects sensitive data even in the approved tool: P50.
units.anchor: we highly recommend against using Bing Copilot on sensitive data sets

units.why: Microsoft AI tool use 'should be consistent with the Information Resources Acceptable Use Policy', tying AI use to existing policy: P77.
units.anchor: use of Microsoft AI tools should be consistent with the

units.why: 'We highly encourage use of the Microsoft products specified above' for official duties points users to the university-contracted tools: P92.
units.anchor: We highly encourage use of the Microsoft products specified above exclusively

units.why: For ChatGPT and similar tools 'only data that is publicly available or defined as Published Data' may be used, a data-protection limit: P50.
units.anchor: Only data that is publicly available or defined as Published Data

units.why: 'Students should always adhere to the UT Tyler Policy on Student Conduct when using any AI tool' applies existing conduct policy to AI: P77.
units.anchor: Students should always adhere to the

units.why: 'Researchers should always adhere to the UT Tyler Policy 3.2.8 Misconduct in Research' defers research AI use to the research-misconduct policy: P62.
units.anchor: Researchers should always adhere to the UT Tyler Policy 3.2.8

units.why: Use of ChatGPT 'cannot include any personal, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information': P50.
units.anchor: cannot include any personal, confidential, proprietary, or otherwise sensitive information

units.why: Names categories (FERPA records, HIPAA information) that 'must not be used with ChatGPT or similar AI Tools': P50.
units.anchor: student records subject to FERPA, health information (HIPAA)

units.why: AI 'must not be used to generate output that would not be considered authorized for public or fair use', a copyright/fair-use limit: P52.
units.anchor: must not be used to generate output that would not be considered authorized

units.why: 'Generating someone else's proprietary or unpublished research' is listed among prohibited examples; an IP restriction, P52.
units.anchor: generating someone else’s proprietary or unpublished research

units.why: 'Legal analysis or advice' is listed as a prohibited AI use, which fits no existing type (not data, IP or academic work).
units.anchor: legal analysis or advice
units.uncovered_note: AI may not be used to produce legal analysis or advice.

units.why: 'Recruitment, personnel or disciplinary decision making' is listed as prohibited AI output, keeping decisions about people with humans: P73.
units.anchor: recruitment, personnel or disciplinary decision making

units.why: AI may not be used for 'completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor', which leaves the allowable manner to each instructor: P04.
units.anchor: completion of academic work in a manner not allowed by the instructor

units.why: Creating 'someone else's proprietary instructional materials without authorized use or proper citations' is prohibited: P52.
units.anchor: creation of someone else’s proprietary instructional materials without authorized use or proper citations

units.why: 'And grading' is on the list of uses for which AI 'must not be used', so humans must grade: P46.
units.anchor: and grading.

units.why: Vendors 'explicitly forbid' fraud and illegal use in their terms, noting tool terms of use: P52, informs.
units.anchor: explicitly forbid their use for certain categories of activity, including fraud and illegal activities

units.why: AI 'may not be used for any activity that would be illegal, fraudulent or a violation of any state or federal law, or UT Tyler or UT System policies': law and policy compliance, P77 rather than P74 which targets specific deceptive acts.
units.anchor: may not be used for any activity that would be illegal, fraudulent

units.why: Defines 'fair use' as a legal doctrine allowing unlicensed use of copyrighted works, background on copyright: P52, informs.
units.anchor: Fair use is a legal doctrine that promotes freedom of expression

units.why: 'Users should not enter any Confidential or Controlled university data in an AI chat tool' protects institutional data: P50.
units.anchor: Users should not enter any Confidential or Controlled university data in an AI chat tool.

units.why: Users 'should always validate the results and verify the sources' of AI output (repeated later; coded once): P31.
units.anchor: Users should always validate the results and verify the sources of information

units.why: 'Users should not violate any policies, including the... Acceptable Use Policy and the specific policies of each AI tool' binds AI use to existing policy: P77.
units.anchor: Users should not violate any policies, including the UT Tyler Information Resources Acceptable Use Policy

units.why: Questions on appropriate AI use go to 'the Information Security Office', naming the office that interprets the policy: P80.
units.anchor: please contact the Information Security Office

units.why: 'All content entered into with, or generated by, ChatGPT is available to... OpenAI, and their employees' warns that prompts are stored: P50.
units.anchor: All content entered into with, or generated by, ChatGPT is available to ChatGPT

units.why: 'There is currently no agreement between UT Tyler and OpenAI' explains why un-vetted tools are risky for data, supporting preference for vetted tools: P50.
units.anchor: no agreement between UT Tyler and OpenAI or other AI Tools

units.why: 'Some data protections are provided through our agreement with Microsoft, but they are limited' qualifies the vetted-tool protection: P50.
units.anchor: Some data protections are provided through our agreement with Microsoft, but they are limited.

units.why: Accepting click-through terms 'without delegated signature authority may face personal consequences': a terms-of-use warning; P52 is nearest.
units.anchor: Individuals who accept click-through agreements without delegated signature authority may face personal consequences
units.fit_note: Concerns personal contractual liability, not copyright or ownership of output.

units.why: Violations 'may result in disciplinary action that may include termination for employees', a concrete penalty stated in advance: P37.
units.anchor: may result in disciplinary action that may include termination for employees and temporaries

units.why: Students may face 'suspension or expulsion', a stated student penalty: P37.
units.anchor: suspension or expulsion in the case of a student

units.why: Individuals 'are subject to loss of University Information Resources access privileges, civil, and criminal prosecution': further stated penalties, P37.
units.anchor: loss of University Information Resources access privileges, civil, and criminal prosecution

notes: Only the two included university-layer documents were coded; no school or computing policy was found and course syllabi were deferred. Legal analysis or advice as a prohibited AI use was coded UNCOVERED.
